title: Pre-Market — Monday, November 16, 2026
html:
AI gets sold before Nvidia speaks, and SPY drifts toward the floor we wanted to buy

Here's what I'm seeing before the bell. Futures are lower, but only the AI and crypto corner is really selling. The Dow is flat and the 2-year yield is down. That's de-risking before Tuesday night, not a market-wide scare.

The one thing

SPY is about $751.70 pre-market (−0.4%), sitting on the 38.2% line ($751.39) and $4.70 above the $747 zone where the $770 call plan buys. If the $744–745 floor holds on a dip, that's the entry we've been waiting for all week.

The selling is narrow. Nasdaq futures are down about 1%, the Dow is flat, and the 2-year yield slipped 2 basis points (a basis point is 0.01%) after its biggest weekly rise in over two years. When rates ease and only one group falls, money is leaving that group, not the market. Here that group is chips, AI hardware and crypto, two days before Nvidia reports without its founder at the top.

What would change my mind: a close below $741, or the selling spreading to the Dow and small caps. Then the floor is failing, not being tested, and we buy nothing.

Overnight, and what it means

  • US futures: S&P 500 −0.36%, Nasdaq 100 −0.97%, Dow +0.02%, Russell 2000 −0.4% (about 5 AM ET). Chips led: Intel, AMD, Broadcom and Micron −3.5% to −5%; Dell −5.1%; Super Micro −3.8%; Nvidia −2.2%.
  • Abroad: Europe's tech names (ASML, Infineon) are the biggest drags on the Stoxx 600. China's October data came in soft, as reported: retail sales +0.4% y/y vs 0.8% expected, factory output +4.8% vs 5.3%. Japan's Q3 GDP was flat. I couldn't confirm clean Asian index closes this morning.
  • Oil: Brent about $95.4–96.3, WTI about $88.3–89.1, roughly flat. That's after Iran hit a US helicopter base in Bahrain on Sunday and Iranian TV said five vessels hit mines in Hormuz. The IEA now sees Q4 supply about 1.7 million barrels a day above demand.
  • Rates, dollar, gold, fear: 2-year yield −2 bp; 10-year about 5.14–5.15%. Dollar index about 103.4. Gold about $3,877, a one-year low. VIX about 19.9 (+3%). Bitcoin about $64,700 (−1%).
  • Fed: Markets fully price a quarter-point hike on Dec 9, with about an 8% chance of a half point. Chair Warsh and Cleveland's Hammack both speak today; no remarks yet.

Iran struck a US base on Sunday, and oil went down. That tells you supply, not headlines, sets the price now, which is good news for DAL's fuel bill and less good for the XOM chase. Put it together: rates eased, oil sat still, and only AI and crypto sold. That confirms last night's force that this market wants proof before it pays up, and it hits the weakest theme, AI infrastructure, hardest. The rates force got a little weaker overnight, not stronger.

SPY at the open (SPY)

Pre-market ≈ $751.70 (estimate).

  • Oct 6 record high: $781.62
  • 78.6% of the drop · target 2: $771.15
  • Ceiling · 61.8% + 50-day · target 1: $763–765
  • 50% of the drop: $757.17
  • 38.2% · Friday low area: $751.39
  • Floor · two 23.6% lines · stop < $741: $744–745
  • 200-day + Nov 5 low: $729–733
  • If SPY opens above $757.17, the dip is already over and SPY is back in the middle of the box. Nothing triggers. The ceiling is still $763–765.
  • If it holds between $747 and $757.17, wait. This is the no-trade middle where the reward-to-risk math fails.
  • If it opens below $747, that's the $770 call's zone, but only once the $744–745 floor holds and price turns back up. A close below $741 ends the idea; no new calls then.

How I read it: the pre-market price sits 31 cents over the 38.2% line ($751.39), the level that marked Friday's low area. Below it is the floor we planned around: two 23.6% lines from two different swings at $744–745. Above, the 61.8% line and the 50-day make the $763–765 ceiling.

Movers on your list (Watchlist)

Webull wasn't connected this morning, so prices below are estimates from the reported % moves and Friday's closes. Verify in Webull before acting.

NamePre%Why
NVDA~$159.30−2.2%FT: Huang and allies discussing a push to reinstate him; reports Tue after the close.
INTC~$57~−4%Proposed class action says Intel misled holders on PC sales and inventory.
AMD~$513~−4%Sold with the chip group into Nvidia.
DELLn/a−5.1%AI hardware selling; reports Nov 24.
SMCIn/a−3.8%Same AI hardware selling.
HOODn/alowerCrypto stocks down as bitcoin touched $64,000.
  • NVDA sits between your 0.5 ($155.33) and your 0.786 ($170.22). No change: no Nvidia option before the report, the Nov 20 options were EXPENSIVE (1.99) on Friday.
  • INTC is pressing toward the 78.6% of its full run (~$56.31). It fits the downtrend, but a gap down on a lawsuit headline is a chase, not a setup. No play.
  • AMD moves away from your 2.0 ceiling ($558.82); your 1.618 ($464.60) is the floor below. No change.
  • DELL and SMH (your downside ideas) are moving your way. DELL reports Nov 24, inside a week of most entries now, so no DELL put. SMH has no play on file.
  • HOOD falling is not the put entry. The plan sells a failed bounce into $81–84, not a drop already underway.
  • PLTR and DAL (your current ideas): no news. PLTR trades with AI software, so expect pressure; its exit is only a close below $158. DAL gets a quiet gift from flat oil.

Today's calendar (ET)

  • 8:30 AM: Empire State manufacturing (November) · 19 expected, prior 25.5. A New York factory survey; a big miss would add to the growth worry.
  • Today: Fed Chair Warsh speaks in San Francisco; Cleveland's Hammack also speaks. Times not confirmed. Listen for whether a half-point hike is on the table.
  • Earnings: Before the open: Tyson Foods, Aramark; Baidu also reports today. No watchlist name or mega-cap reports today or tonight, so no IV-crush risk overnight.
  • Ahead: Tue: retail sales (8:30), Home Depot, then Nvidia after the close. Wed: FOMC minutes 2:00 PM. Thu: Walmart; Anthropic's IPO is expected (calendar note only: Claude is made by Anthropic, so no view on it). Holding any Nvidia option through Tuesday night means IV crush: the extra premium drains right after the report.

Plays check (Options Playbook)

Option quotes are Friday's closing marks (options don't trade before the bell), so check them live at the open. "IV vs moves" compares the option's implied volatility with the stock's actual 60-day moves: under 0.9 CHEAP, over 1.25 EXPENSIVE. No earnings sit inside any of these contracts.

  • SPY Dec 18 $770 call (watching) · Closer to triggering. $4.70 above the $747 zone. Enter on a dip that holds $744–745; stop a close below $741; targets $763, then $771.15. From $747 that's still 2.7 to 1 to target 1. OI 37,192 · bid/ask $6.20/$6.30 · ≈ $396 at the entry (estimate) · IV 13% vs moves 15% → CHEAP
  • PLTR Dec 18 $180 call (open) · Still valid. Entry $757.50, marked $577.50. Exit only on a close below $158. Your 1.382 ($167.37) is the line to watch on the 3-day close. AI software is under pressure this morning; don't add. OI 8,727 · bid/ask $5.65/$5.90 · IV 47% vs moves 50% → FAIR
  • DAL Dec 18 $90 call (open) · Still valid. Entry $632.50, marked $261.50. Stop: DAL below $83, which is your 2.0 ($83.03). Flat oil helps a little. Hold to the stop; no adding. OI 3,167 · bid/ask $2.46/$2.77 (11.9%, wide: use a limit near the mid to exit) · IV 38% vs moves 37% → FAIR
  • HLT Dec 18 $380 call (open) · Still valid. Entry ~$760, marked $755. Pinned under your 3.0 ($375.22). Exit on a close under $359.41. OI 265 · bid/ask $6.40/$8.70 (thin, 30%: limit orders only) · IV 24% vs moves 23% → FAIR
  • XOM Dec 18 $170 call (watching) · Wait. Buy zone: a dip to $168 or lower that holds your 2.0 ($166.89). Stop a close below $166.50; targets your 2.382 $174.69, then 2.618 $179.51. Flat oil makes a dip more likely, not less. OI 9,048 · bid/ask $5.80/$6.00 · ≈ $480 at the entry (estimate) · IV 27.5% vs moves 26.5% → FAIR
  • V Dec 18 $440 call (watching) · Wait. Trigger: V above $430.18. Stop a close below $423 (just under your 2.382). Targets $442.75, then $473.89. Visa is on the steadier side of today's tape. OI 921 · bid/ask $5.45/$6.00 (9.6%, at the limit) · IV 21% vs moves 22% → FAIR

Also watching, no change: BA $170 put (wait for a failed rally into $179–181.5; stop a close above $185; IV 31% vs moves 35% → CHEAP; its 10-day limit is Friday). KO $100 call (wait for KO above $99.30; a flat Dow and a defensive tape help; IV 19.5%, realized vol not on file, so verify the label in Webull). HOOD $75 put (wait for a failed bounce into $81–84; IV 64.8%, verify the label).

If every open play hit its stop today, the total lost would be about $1,443 from what we paid (estimate from each contract's IV).

No new plays. The overnight moves are gaps in names with earnings close by (Nvidia Tue, Dell Nov 24) or lawsuit headlines (Intel). None is a setup that passes the rules this morning.

Alerts for today

  • SPY — price crosses below $747.00 → $770 call zone (the $744 floor must hold)
  • SPY — price crosses below $741.00 → stop line for that idea (needs a close); no new calls
  • SPY — price crosses above $757.17 → the dip is over; back in the middle, nothing to do
  • XOM — price crosses below $168.00 → buy zone over your 2.0 ($166.89)
  • DAL — price crosses below $83.00 → stop on the open $90 call

An alert means look now, not buy now.

Opening rule of the day: Don't buy the first red candle.

A Nasdaq-led gap down will likely push SPY toward $747 early. Touching $747 is not the entry. Give it 15–30 minutes, and buy only if the $744–745 floor holds and SPY turns back up. Use limit orders at the mid; on DAL and HLT, wide spreads make market orders expensive.

Sources: Reuters via Yahoo Finance (futures, chip moves, Fed pricing, 2-year yield, Nov 16); Yahoo Finance live blog (Huang FT report, Empire State consensus, oil); FinanceFeeds (Brent/WTI, Bahrain strike, IEA, gold, dollar); The Rio Times (10-year, dollar index, China and Japan data, verify); Seeking Alpha (Intel class action, crypto stocks); Finwire (Europe tech). Option quotes, IV vs 60-day moves and stop-value estimates: the Nov 15 Week Ahead and the play scorecard (Nov 13 closing marks). Webull was not connected for this run.

Educational research only, not personalized investment advice. Claude never places trades.
